subject: surgery
title: Hepatic anatomy, benign liver lesions, hepatocellular carcinoma, and hepatic resection
refs: Blumgart's Surgery of the Liver, Biliary Tract and Pancreas

steps.tx: Hepatic **segmental** anatomy is defined by the Couinaud classification, which divides the liver into eight functionally independent segments. Each segment possesses an autonomous triad of portal vein, hepatic artery, and biliary drainage, bounded peripherally by the three main hepatic veins. The Cantlie line, extending from the gallbladder fossa to the inferior vena cava, divides the liver into functional right and left hemilivers, distinct from the anatomical falciform ligament.
steps.say: Couinaud segmental anatomy divides the liver into eight independent segments, each supplied by an autonomous portal triad. The Cantlie line runs from the gallbladder fossa to the inferior vena cava, marking the true functional division between right and left hemilivers.

steps.tx: Benign **hepatic** neoplasms require precise cross-sectional characterization to guide surgical resection versus observation. Cavernous hemangioma is the most common benign liver tumor, demonstrating peripheral nodular puddling on arterial phase with centripetal fill-in on delayed contrast CT. Focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH) is a hyperplastic polyclonal response to vascular malformation, displaying a pathognomonic central stellate scar that enhances on delayed imaging; FNH carries zero malignant potential and requires no resection.
steps.say: Benign liver lesions are differentiated by contrast enhancement. Hemangiomas show peripheral nodular puddling with delayed fill-in. Focal nodular hyperplasia displays a central stellate scar without malignant potential, managed conservatively without resection.

steps.tx: Hepatic **adenoma** is strongly associated with oral contraceptive pills and anabolic steroid usage. Unlike FNH, adenomas harbor significant risks of spontaneous catastrophic intraperitoneal rupture and malignant transformation into hepatocellular carcinoma. Surgical resection is indicated for all adenomas in males, lesions larger than 5 cm in females, beta-catenin mutated subtypes, or lesions failing to regress following contraceptive cessation. Contrast-enhanced MRI is the diagnostic imaging modality of choice.
steps.say: Hepatic adenomas are linked to estrogen and steroid exposure, carrying risks of life-threatening rupture and malignant transformation. Surgical resection is indicated for tumors in men, lesions over five centimeters, beta-catenin mutations, or persistent adenomas.

steps.tx: Hepatocellular **carcinoma** (HCC) staging determines eligibility for surgical resection versus liver transplantation using the Milan criteria. For cirrhotic patients without macroscopic vascular invasion or extrahepatic spread, orthotopic liver transplantation achieves superior disease-free survival if within Milan limits: a single lesion up to 5 cm or up to three lesions none exceeding 3 cm. Non-cirrhotic patients or Child-Pugh A cirrhotics without portal hypertension are candidates for partial hepatectomy.
steps.say: Hepatocellular carcinoma in cirrhosis is triaged by the Milan criteria for liver transplantation: one tumor up to five centimeters or up to three tumors each under three centimeters. Non-cirrhotic patients with preserved liver function are candidates for anatomical hepatectomy.
